subject: Invoice discrepancy after Patchwork acquisition — split requested
messages:
From: Ellen Zhou <ellen.zhou@patchworklabs.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwoodinference.com, billing@redwoodinference.com
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Invoice #RL-202705 - charges post-Patchwork acquisition

Hi Maya / Redwood billing team,

We closed on the acquisition of QuickScale on Apr 28 and our finance team just received the May invoice (attached). It looks like charges for both Patchwork and QuickScale were billed to the same account and aggregated on line items — we expected a post-close separation so each legal entity is billed to its own ledger for tax reporting.

Quick summary: 1) The invoice shows a ~14% bump vs expected (mostly streaming tokens on evenings) 2) The entries include two API keys and three service prefixes but were combined into a single line which makes VAT allocation unclear 3) We need a split by tenant/entity (Patchwork Labs vs QuickScale Inc.) for our bookkeeping and VAT reclaim process.

Can you confirm: a) whether you can retroactively split the May invoice by customer entity and provide a supporting CSV with token-by-prefix attribution, and b) any VAT implications we should expect if you issue a credit and two new invoices?

I've attached our internal acquisition MOU and a screenshot of the billing portal that highlights the merged ledger. If you prefer a quick call, our CFO (Laura) is available tomorrow morning PST.

Thanks — appreciate the quick help here.

— Ellen
Ellen Zhou
Head of Finance, Patchwork Labs
ellen.zhou@patchworklabs.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: invoice-RL-202705.pdf (pdf), acquisition-mou.pdf (pdf)

From: maya_srinivasan@redwoodinference.com
To: Ellen Zhou <ellen.zhou@patchworklabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter, kimberly_park, david_kim
Date: 2027-05-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice #RL-202705 - charges post-Patchwork acquisition

Hi Ellen — thanks for flagging and congrats on the close. Looping in Ben (billing ops) and Kim (tax & VAT) to take the lead.

Short answer: we can run a retroactive allocation and issue corrected invoice artifacts, but I want to make sure we do this cleanly to avoid double VAT exposure. Ben — can your team extract token-by-prefix attribution for the billing window Apr 28–May 31 and produce a CSV we can send to the customer? Please include: api_key, prefix, start_ts, end_ts, token_in, token_out, model, estimated_cost_usd.

Kim — can you advise on VAT treatment if we issue a credit and then two reissued invoices (one per legal entity) versus issuing adjustments on our ledger (single invoice with internal memo)? Patchwork has EU customers so they will need reclaimable evidence.

Ellen — we'll target an initial data packet by EOD Tues (2027-05-18) and aim to have draft invoice adjustments by end of week. If you can share the list of which prefixes map to QuickScale vs Patchwork that will speed things up — otherwise Ben will correlate by API key.

Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Head of Customer Finance, Redwood Inference
maya.srinivasan@redwoodinference.com

Date: 2027-05-17T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice #RL-202705 - charges post-Patchwork acquisition

Thanks Maya — quick ops note and plan below.

Plan: 1) I pulled a usage snapshot for the invoice window (attached usage-snapshot-202704.json) and ran prefix correlation. There are three prefixes: pw-prod, qs-prod, qs-staging. Of those, qs-staging was supposed to be billed to QuickScale but was erroneously mapped to Patchwork main account during the account merge. 2) I exported per-request token counts and aggregated to a CSV (attached merged-ledger-202704.csv). Column set: api_key, prefix, request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, timestamp, region. 3) Next steps: confirm prefix-to-entity mapping with Ellen; then we can generate two adjusted invoices (credit + two invoices) and produce VAT evidence per entity.

Ellen — I'm attaching the CSV extract. Can you confirm that qs-prod and qs-staging belong to QuickScale Inc., and pw-prod belongs to Patchwork Labs? If you confirm, we'll proceed to draft credit/invoice documents and circulate to Kim for VAT language.

Notes:  - There is a small number (~0.6%) of requests with missing request_id due to an internal proxy rewrite during the migration window; I flagged those in the CSV with request_id=__MIGRATION_PROXY__ and recommend we allocate those to QuickScale if they map to qs-* prefixes.

Ben Carter
Billing Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: merged-ledger-202704.csv (csv)

From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
To: maya_srinivasan@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, Ellen Zhou <ellen.zhou@patchworklabs.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-18T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice #RL-202705 - charges post-Patchwork acquisition

Hi all — tax perspective and proposed wording for invoice artifacts.

VAT/Treatment: 1) If Redwood issues a full credit for the aggregated May invoice and reissues two invoices (one with Patchwork Labs VAT registration and one with QuickScale Inc.), each invoice will show the net usage for that legal entity and the VAT will be applied using the registration provided for each. That is the cleanest approach for client reclaim. 2) If instead we adjust internally and leave a single invoice with an allocation memo, Patchwork will face extra work to split the reclaim on their side; we should only do that if the customer explicitly requests it.

Suggested artifact set (we will produce):
- Credit note referencing original invoice RL-202705 (reason: allocation error).
- Invoice RL-202705-A for Patchwork Labs (net amounts, VAT as specified).
- Invoice RL-202705-B for QuickScale Inc.
- Supporting CSV (merged-ledger-202704.csv) and summary PDF with token totals per entity.

Kimberly Park
Head of Tax & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
